topics.label: Lecture introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by framing complement as an essential yet structurally complex topic in immunology.

topics.label: Core principles and nomenclature of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overview of the complement system's general architecture and explain its standard naming conventions.

topics.label: C3 activation and the three complement pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the central biochemical role of C3 and detail how the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways generate convertases to trigger activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes activated by complement to eliminate pathogens through opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host tissue protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent self-damage by dampening complement activation on host cells.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations, infection risks, and autoimmune conditions caused by specific complement component deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to subvert complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture session and previews the subsequent topic on the adaptive immune system.
